previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 20%), atrial fibrillation, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening left-sided back pain and found to have acute on chronic kidney injury. Imaging ruled out aortic graft leak but showed degenerative spinal changes likely contributing to musculoskeletal back pain. His elevated creatinine, from a baseline of 1.6 to 2.5, was attributed to pre-renal azotemia from uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c 10.1%). He was managed with gentle hydration, temporary discontinuation of torsemide and warfarin, and optimization of insulin therapy. His insulin regimen was increased to 75 units of 70/30 before breakfast and 50 units before dinner. He received counseling on diet and diabetes management, and his kidney function improved. He was discharged home with stable vital signs, a referral to physical therapy for back pain, and instructions to monitor daily weights and follow up with his primary care and cardiology providers.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 30%), atrial 
fibrillation on warfarin, CKD and restrictive lung disease was 
admitted with 2 days of dyspnea at rest, cough, headache, sore 
throat, most likely representing acute viral URI in the setting 
of chronic restrictive lung disease.

ACUTE ISSUES:
===========
# Chronic restrictive lung disease with acute viral URI: Pt was 
admitted with 2 days of dyspnea at rest, cough, headache, sore 
throat, most likely representing viral upper respiratory tract 
infection in the setting of known 
restrictive lung disease. He was initially treated with 
scheduled albuterol and ipratropium nebulizers, prednisone, and 
levofloxacin (QTc prolonging interaction with amiodarone and 
azithromycin). Antibiotics were discontinued after chart 
research revealed that pt does NOT have PFTs consistent with 
COPD.  Pulmonary was consulted, and it was determined that pt 
has restrictive lung disease consistent with ILD and asbestosis. 
 Possible etiologies other than asbestos exposure include a 
history of spray painting without face mask and long term 
amiodarone treatment.  Rheumatologic workup was negative ___ 
1:40, anti-scl 70 negative, anti-Ro/La negative). Pt did have 
wheezes during his course, most likely ___ reactive airway 
disease in the setting of URI, and improved symptomatically with 
nebs and a five day course of prednisone.  On discharge, pt was 
oxygenating well on room air, and did not desaturate with 
ambulation.  Pt will follow up with Dr. ___ of 
pulmonology as an outpatient.  In addition, pt will have an 
outpatient follow up CT chest to reassess pt's known pulmonary 
nodule per plan with Thoracic Surgery.  Pt's cardiologist, Dr. 
___, was emailed regarding the possibility of 
discontinuing amiodarone given its possible contribution to pt's 
lung disease, however there was no reply prior to discharge.     


# Acute on chronic kidney disease: On presentation, pt's Cr was 
found to be 2.2, up from a baseline of 1.5. This initial 
increase likely represented prerenal acute on chronic kidney 
disease from mild CHF.  Pt's Cr improved initially with 
diuresis.  However, pt's diuresis was continued and Cr rose from 
2.0 to 2.7 secondary to over-diuresis.  Pt's Cr improved toward 
baseline once diuresis was held and IV fluids were administered. 
 On discharge pt's Cr had improved to 2.3, and pt's home 
Torsemide was held with the plan that pt would follow up with 
his PCP on ___ and the decision whether or not to 
resume diuresis would be made based on clinical exam and chem 7.

# Mild acute on chronic systolic heart failure: Pt initially 
presented with minor crackles on lung exam, JVP not 
significantly elevated and BNP at an indeterminate level of 650. 
 Pt was mildly volume overloaded, but pt's presenting symptoms 
were likely not related.  Pt was diuresed as described above.  
Pt was continued on his home torsemide 40mg initially, but it 
was held once pt developed ___ secondary to over-diuresis.  Pt's 
aspirin, statin, spironolactone and beta blocker were continued. 
 On presentation, pt was not on an ACE inhibitor.  Pt was 
previously on lisinopril 2.5mg daily in ___, but was taken off 
due to acute kidney injury.  Resumption of an ACE inhibitor 
should be considered once pt's renal function stabilizes given 
the survival benefit.

============
# Non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: Unclear etiology.  TTE in ___ 
demonstrated a left ventricular LVEF of 25%.  Pt's home heart 
failure regimen was continued as described above. Repeat TTE 
this hospitalization showed a borderline dilated left ventricle 
with moderate global left ventricular hypokinesis (LVEF of 30%) 
largely unchanged from previous TTE.

# Type 2 Diabetes: Pt's home insulin regimen was continued.  

# Atrial fibrillation: Pt presented with an INR of 2.1, and 
coumadin and amiodarone were continued.    

# Depression: Pt's imipramine, mirtazapine and perphenazine were 
continued.
